findings: No new dependency, network call, shell invocation or eval was added in the diff of anvil/ and tools/; changes use the standard library only.

Approver change fails closed: an expected reviewer that failed or was not counted yields human_required with the stations named, and human_required is now a recognised verdict. This removes the silent approve default.

Builder report validation is strict exact substring containment, refuses a runner-saved transcript as the report when literals are required, and unlinks a stale builder.output.md before each attempt, so a stale file cannot stand in. Residual and accepted: a builder that writes the literal text without doing the work still passes this deterministic check, so reviewers remain the semantic control.

Reviewer tree guard was widened (own_prefix) to allow runs/<wo>/<station>.* single-level files. The scope is limited to the station's own namespace under runs/, with no subdirectories, and every other changed path still fails the guard. Low risk; note that the wrapper trusts work_order_id and station values for building the prefix, which come from the packet and not from model output.

Required literals from the work order are written into the builder prompt with control characters sanitized. Work order text can originate from a GitHub issue, so it is untrusted prompt input, but this is the same trust level as the existing description field. No change requested.
Protected paths (pipelines/, existing tests) are not modified, and the protected-path gate and review parse contract are untouched. No secrets, credentials or unsafe defaults were introduced.
